en.title: Lanterns Reveals John's Grueling Green Lantern Audition
en.summary: The latest episode of Lanterns dives deep into the origins of John's recruitment into the Green Lantern Corps. We witness a bizarre and demanding interview process that tests his sanity and resolve.
en.body:
The universe of **Lanterns** continues to expand, and the latest installment, "OutKast," takes us back in time to shed crucial light on how **John** became the Green Lantern we know. While the episode might be out of chronological order, its impact is undeniable, providing essential backstory that deepens our understanding of his journey.

We find John in a disorienting situation, falling through an abandoned shopping mall before being directed to a backroom office. There, he meets **Lianna** (played by **Laura Linney**), one of the enigmatic Guardians. She presents him with an unconventional interview for a potential position within the Green Lantern Corps. The test is simple yet severe: wait. John adheres to this directive with an almost unnerving seriousness, remaining in the office for a full day and night. Lianna's surprise the next morning at his unwavering dedication highlights the unusual nature of the recruitment process.

This intense vetting is designed to gauge more than just physical prowess; it probes the candidate's resilience and perception of reality. When questioned about a prior, terrifying experience—being trapped in an alien bubble and awoken in the middle of the night—John admits he was afraid. This honesty, coupled with his insistence that the surreal event was real, leads others, including his wife **Bernadette** (**Jasmine Cephas Jones**), to believe he might be losing his mind. Bernadette is on the verge of ostracization when Lianna intervenes, attempting to smooth over the rough edges of the selection process and hinting that other candidates faced similarly bewildering trials.

## The Cost of Becoming a Guardian

The "OutKast" episode is a masterclass in character development, illustrating that joining the Green Lantern Corps is not merely about wielding a ring; it's about enduring psychological trials that would break lesser individuals. The Guardians' methods, as depicted through Lianna's interview with John, are deliberately extreme. They seek individuals who can not only confront cosmic threats but also maintain their grip on reality when faced with the incomprehensible. John's unwavering belief in his own experience, even when it isolates him from his loved ones, proves his mettle in a way that brute strength never could. It’s a stark reminder that the most compelling stories often lie in the personal struggles of their heroes.

## Fan Reactions to John's Origin

Fans on social media and forums have been abuzz discussing the implications of "OutKast." Many are praising the show for delving into the character’s formative experiences, arguing that this level of detail is what sets **Lanterns** apart from other superhero narratives. The portrayal of John’s isolation and the strain on his marriage resonates deeply, with viewers sharing their appreciation for the show’s willingness to explore the emotional toll of his cosmic calling. The unique and somewhat unsettling interview process has also sparked considerable debate, with many agreeing that it effectively showcases the Guardians' peculiar standards for selecting their Lanterns.

## What's Next for the Corps

With this crucial piece of John's history now revealed, the stage is set for further exploration of his integration into the Green Lantern Corps. Future episodes are expected to build upon this foundation, showing how this rigorous initiation shapes his actions and decisions as he patrols his sector. The dynamic between John and the Guardians is sure to evolve as they recognize his unique brand of resilience.

This time around? We get to find out how John was approached for his shiny new gig. Recap Image: John Johnson/HBO Max John falls many stories through an abandoned shopping mall onto a pile of mattresses. There’s an arrow pointing upstairs, and he eventually makes his way into a backroom office where Lianna (Laura Linney) awaits. She tells John to have a seat and wait, then leaves. John stays in the office all day and overnight; Lianna is surprised to find that he took the directive so seriously when she returns the next morning. She is one of the Guardians, here to interview him about a new possible position opening up in the Green Lantern Corps. In order to do this, she needs more information on his life and when he was questioned—after being awoken in the middle of the night, and trapped inside an alien bubble—he answered that of course he was afraid, and consequently was not selected. His insistence that the experience was real has everyone believing he’s lost his mind, including his wife Bernadette (Jasmine Cephas Jones). She nearly kicks him out of the house, but is approached by Lianna, who tries to make recompense for the interviewing process—other candidates apparently had similar ill-effects. Bernadette tells Lianna off for not knowing anything about race relations on Earth and expecting no fear from a Black man in America. Lianna apologizes for the misunderstanding and notes that perhaps John Jr. might be suitable to wield the ring in the future. Bernadette tells her husband that this is their most important project, raising John to know no fear. Bernadette and John Sr. tell John about this “destiny” when he (Jayce Eiland) turns five years old, getting him a lantern costume for his birthday instead of the crayons he asked for. She tells him that the birds are watching and serve as messengers to the Guardians, and also has satellite equipment in the house to reach them. John’s training is increasingly harsh, from shooting apples off his head to having him walk home through crime-laden neighborhoods, with only cheeseburgers as reward. He never really gets time off, and his brothers resent him for how differently he’s treated, telling John that he sounds like a white boy.
